{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"6187475dd6fd21f756397b54389b121601e618f4dd11965c586892894faf1a7d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Revocation, suspension and driver improvement","heading":"C2 — Revocation, suspension and driver improvement","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Revocation, suspension and driver improvement

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A03
At eight calculated points, the DMV sends the driver an advisory letter. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A03
At 12 calculated points, the driver must complete a behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course within 90 days of notification unless the DMV grants an extension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A03
At the 12-point program level, noncompliance with the course requirement or the driver’s preference results in a mandatory two-month suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A03
The action table assigns a mandatory four-month suspension at 14 calculated points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A03
The action table assigns a mandatory six-month suspension at 16 calculated points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A03
The action table assigns a mandatory eight-month suspension at 18 calculated points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A03
The action table assigns a mandatory 10-month suspension at 20 calculated points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A03
Reinstatement following the listed 14-, 16-, 18- or 20-point suspension requires completion of a behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course within the preceding two years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A04
The action table assigns a mandatory 12-month suspension at 22 calculated points. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A04
Reinstatement after the 22-point suspension requires a behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course completed within the preceding two years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A04
For a Class D driver’s first speeding violation within three years at 1 through 14 mph above the limit, points are avoided only if payment is through the Voluntary Assessment Center or Alderman’s Court recorded as guilty mail-in, or through online payment. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A04
A speeding conviction for 20 through 24 mph above the posted limit leads to an advisory letter. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A04
A conviction for driving 25 mph above the limit brings an initial one-month suspension, with another month added for each further five mph above that threshold. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A04
A driver convicted of speeding 25 through 29 mph above the limit may choose the behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course instead of suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A04
At 30 mph or more above the posted limit, suspension is mandatory and reinstatement requires the behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course within the preceding two years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A04
A conviction for driving at least 50 mph above the limit or driving 100 mph on a highway brings a one-year suspension and requires the approved course within the preceding two years for reinstatement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A04
The DMV may issue an occupational license for extreme hardship during a Problem Driver Program suspension unless other Title 21 convictions also cause suspension or revocation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A04
An occupational license is unavailable after two prior suspensions under the policy within three years or an occupational license issued within the previous 12 months. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A04
An occupational license is not issued during the first month of suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A04
When calculated points reach at least 15 within 24 months, an occupational license is withheld until the calculated total falls below 15. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A04
A conviction for violating occupational-license restrictions adds an equal suspension period and requires surrender of the occupational license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A05
A conviction for driving during suspension or revocation adds an equal withdrawal period, limited to one year. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A05
No driving authority is allowed during the remainder of the original suspension or revocation or during its extension, and previously issued authority must be surrendered. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A05
A continuous episode producing convictions for at least three aggressive-driving traffic offenses, such as speeding, unsafe lane changes or following too closely, meets the handbook’s aggressive-driving definition. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A05
The first aggressive-driving offense carries a fine from $100 to $300. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A05
An aggressive-driving conviction requires completion of the behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course within 90 days. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A05
Failure to attend the required aggressive-driving course results in suspension of driving privileges. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R28 | anchor: A05
The approved behavior-modification or attitudinal-driving course lasts at least eight hours and is offered in all three Delaware counties. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R29 | anchor: A05
The handbook states that the behavior-modification course costs $100, payable to the course provider. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R30 | anchor: A05
After course completion, the provider sends electronic completion notice to the DMV within 48 hours. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R31 | anchor: A05
The DMV may treat successful completion of an approved defensive-driving course as a three-point credit for calculating administrative driver penalties. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R32 | anchor: A05
The defensive-driving credit is used only for administrative action on future violations and does not erase existing DMV points or reduce the full-value total used for employment or insurance review. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R33 | anchor: A05
An approved defensive-driving course remains valid for three years after completion. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-R34 | anchor: A05
Even a small amount of alcohol increases crash risk compared with drinking no alcohol. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0049]
